take:
n8n is an open-source workflow automation tool, and across these 8 posts it is mostly framed as a self-hosted Zapier. One curated summary describes AI-powered LinkedIn content pipelines, email summarizers, lead enrichment and content repurposing, with a Docker setup and example JSON workflows [self-hosted Zapier](/e/2b29777c0b5a). A list of open-source SaaS replacements names n8n as the Zapier alternative and notes that self-hosting removes per-task pricing, though that post's price comparisons look inflated [open-source replacements](/e/DY-6VBpEgLS). Cal.com, Bitwarden and Whisper each co-occur in 2 posts, mainly because of lists like this one.

The most concrete build is @koen.agi's: a Telegram message becomes an eight-part story, each part rendered with Veo 3, stitched together and uploaded to YouTube automatically [Telegram to YouTube vlog](/e/DLypfhGRhKw). It is a demo only; the actual guide is behind a comment-for-link.

Claude Code appears in 3 posts. @chase.h.ai recommends czlonkowski/n8n-mcp, which the caption says gives Claude Code knowledge of all 1,084 n8n nodes so it can build workflows [seven repos](/e/DUzg0n1jRK-). @angus.sewell lists n8n as his go-to for automation in the short list of tools he actually pays for [paid tool stack](/e/DUODsbFkTC3). See the [Claude mastery guide](/guides/claude-mastery) for the wider Claude setup.

The evidence is thin. In several posts n8n is incidental: a Claude Projects video whose transcript is about custom MCP tools, not n8n [Claude Projects agents](/e/DVL-uyCkb5a), a rapid tier list of agent-first tools where most names are not recoverable [agent-first tools](/e/DW6ZoqNERB4), and an influencer roast that only mentions someone "playing with N8N" at 3 a.m. [influencer roast](/e/DUWoNrtEpEu). The archive shows what n8n is used for, not how it holds up in practice.
